title: Classic Paneer Tikka
description: Tender cottage cheese cubes marinated in spiced yogurt, skewered with bell peppers and onions, and charred to perfection.
instructions: Cut paneer, bell pepper, and onion into 1-inch squares.
In a bowl, mix yogurt, mustard oil, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, and salt.
Toss the paneer and vegetables in the marinade and let it rest for 20 minutes.
Skew the paneer cubes alternately with onion and bell pepper pieces.
Grill in an oven or on a hot tawa for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally until charred on the edges.
Sprinkle chaat masala and squeeze fresh lemon juice on top before serving.

title: Malabar Fish Curry
description: A traditional coastal Kerala style fish curry simmered in raw coconut milk, sour tamarind, and warm spices.
instructions: Heat oil in a deep pan, add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and sliced onion, sautéing until soft.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chopped tomato, cooking until the tomato is mushy.
Add tamarind paste, turmeric powder, and salt. Pour in 1 cup of water and bring to a simmer.
Gently place the fish fillets in the gravy and cook on medium-low heat for 6-8 minutes.
Pour in the fresh coconut milk, swirl the pan gently (do not use a spoon to avoid breaking the fish), and simmer for 2 minutes on low heat.
Serve warm with steamed basmati rice.

title: Dal Baati Churma
description: A classic Rajasthani three-in-one meal featuring baked whole wheat dough balls (baati), mixed spiced lentils (dal), and sweet churma.
instructions: To make Baatis: Knead wheat flour with ghee, salt, and warm water into a tight dough. Shape into round balls and bake in a tandoor or preheated oven at 190°C for 30 minutes until golden.
To make Dal: Pressure cook the yellow lentils with turmeric and salt. Temper with ghee, cumin seeds, grated ginger, and red chilies in a separate pan, then combine with the dal.
To make Churma: Crush 2 baked baatis into a fine powder. Sauté in ghee for 2 minutes, let it cool, and mix in sugar and cardamom powder.
Dip the hot baatis in melted ghee and serve along with the hot spiced dal and sweet churma.

title: Kolkata Fish Fry
description: Crispy, golden Bengali street snack of breaded fish fillets marinated in coriander-mint green paste and deep fried.
instructions: Blend cilantro, green chili, ginger, and garlic into a smooth green paste.
Marinate fish fillets with green paste, lemon juice, and salt for 30 minutes.
Beat the egg in a bowl. Spread breadcrumbs on a flat plate.
Dip each marinated fish fillet in the egg wash, then coat generously with breadcrumbs, pressing to form a flat cutlet shape.
Heat cooking oil in a deep pan. Deep fry the breaded cutlets on medium heat until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
Serve hot with kasundi (mustard sauce) and onion rings.

title: Awadhi Dum Biryani
description: A majestic and highly fragrant royal rice dish layered with marinated chicken, saffron milk, and aromatic basmati rice.
instructions: Wash and soak basmati rice for 30 minutes, then parboil until 70% cooked and drain.
Marinate chicken cubes with yogurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for 1 hour.
Deep fry sliced onions until crispy and brown (birista). Set aside.
Cook marinated chicken in a pot with ghee until tender. Layer parboiled rice on top of the chicken.
Sprinkle fried onions, fresh mint leaves, ghee, and saffron-infused milk over the rice layer.
Seal the pot with dough or a tight lid and cook on lowest heat (dum) for 15-20 minutes until rice is fully fluffy.
Gently fluff the biryani and serve hot with raita.

title: Classic Tiffin Set
description: A comforting traditional South Indian breakfast combo featuring soft steamed idlis, crispy urad dal vadas, and hot lentil sambar.
instructions: To make Idlis: Pour fermented rice batter into greased idli molds and steam for 10-12 minutes.
To make Sambar: Cook yellow lentils with chopped drumsticks, tomatoes, tamarind, and sambar powder until soft.
To make Coconut Chutney: Blend grated coconut, roasted gram, green chilies, and salt. Temper with oil, mustard seeds, and curry leaves.
Plate the hot idlis and vadas together and serve with warm sambar and coconut chutney.

title: Aromatic Jeera Rice
description: Fragrant steamed basmati rice tempered with cumin seeds and real ghee. Perfect with Dal Tadka.
instructions: Wash the basmati rice in cold water three times, then soak for 20 minutes and drain.
Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the drained rice and sauté gently for 1-2 minutes in the ghee.
Pour in water and add salt to taste. Bring it to a boil.
Cover with a tight lid, reduce heat to lowest setting, and cook for 12-15 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let it rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork before serving.

title: Garlic Butter Naan
description: Soft and chewy restaurant-style flatbread brushed with garlic-infused butter, cooked on a hot skillet.
instructions: Combine flour, yogurt, a pinch of baking powder, salt, and warm water to knead a soft dough.
Cover dough with a damp cloth and let it rise/rest for 1 hour.
Divide into equal balls. Flatten and roll each ball into an oval teardrop shape.
Sprinkle finely minced garlic and fresh coriander leaves on one side, pressing them into the dough.
Heat a tawa or heavy iron skillet. Wet the back side of the naan with water and slap it onto the skillet (water helps it stick).
Once bubbles appear, flip the tawa upside down directly over the flame to char the garlic side.
Scrape off the naan, brush generously with melted butter, and serve hot.

title: Spiced Masala Chai
description: The quintessential Indian milk tea brewed with crushed fresh ginger, cardamom pods, and strong black tea leaves.
instructions: Boil water in a saucepan. Add crushed ginger and slightly crushed cardamom pods, simmering for 2 minutes to extract flavors.
Add black tea leaves and sugar. Let the water boil for another minute.
Pour in the milk and bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
Once it boils, reduce heat to low and simmer for 2 minutes until it develops a rich caramel-brown color.
Strain the hot masala chai through a sieve directly into cups and serve with biscuits.

title: Dhaba Style Dal Tadka
description: Creamy yellow lentils (toor dal) cooked with spices and tempered with ghee, cumin seeds, garlic, and red chilies.
instructions: Wash yellow lentils. Pressure cook or boil them in water with turmeric powder and salt until soft.
In a pan, heat ghee. Add cumin seeds and chopped garlic. Sauté until garlic turns golden brown.
Add chopped onions and fry until translucent. Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour the boiled dal into the pan, mix well, and bring to a simmer. Adjust salt and thickness with water.
For the final tempering (tadka): Heat a spoonful of ghee in a tiny pan, add cumin, dried red chili, and pour it sizzling over the dal.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with jeera rice.
